system.name: Q-RAG
system.one_liner: A retrieval method that fine-tunes the embedder with value-based reinforcement learning so an agent picks chunks of a long context step by step using learned Q-values.

content.variant_note: an agent box above and an environment box below a row of document chunks, closed into a loop by arrows around the figure, with one step shown on a toy story
content.argues: Multi-step retrieval is an RL episode: the agent embeds the state and every chunk, scores each chunk with a Q-function, a policy picks the next chunk, and the environment returns the reward and the extended state.
content.subject: Q-RAG agent with state and action embedders, Q values and policy, a row of document chunks, and the environment with critic and next state.

elements.name: Q-RAG Agent
elements.role: the learner that embeds the state and the chunks and selects the next chunk
elements.drawn_as: large white rounded box with a thick green outline and a grey title above

elements.name: State Embedder
elements.role: embeds the current state, the query plus all previously selected chunks
elements.drawn_as: pale green rounded box with a thin green outline

elements.name: Action Embedder
elements.role: embeds each chunk of the long context once at the start of the episode
elements.drawn_as: pale green rounded box below the state embedder

elements.name: e_st, e_c0 ... e_c5
elements.role: state embedding and chunk embeddings; a × stands where the embedding of the selected chunk c4 would be
elements.drawn_as: italic serif symbols on green connectors; vertical stubs from the action embedder

elements.name: Q values
elements.role: utility of retrieving each chunk, Qθ(st, c0) to Qθ(st, c5)
elements.drawn_as: very pale green box with two formulas and a column of dots between them, grey caption above

elements.name: π(·|st)
elements.role: policy that picks the next chunk with probability proportional to its Q value
elements.drawn_as: large serif formula at the end of a green arrow from the Q values

elements.name: at = c3
elements.role: the selected action, chunk c3, with its text
elements.drawn_as: large serif equation at the right with a yellow note below it reading '...that, he spent twenty minutes at a café...'

elements.name: st = q {c4}
elements.role: current state: the query q and the previously selected chunk c4
elements.drawn_as: equation with a pink note chip for q and a grey note chip for c4 inside braces

elements.name: Long-Context Document
elements.role: the long text split into chunks c0 to c5 that the agent searches
elements.drawn_as: curly brace around a row of six sticky-note chunks, grey caption at the right

elements.name: chunk notes c0-c5
elements.role: text snippets of a story about John (office, home, pharmacy, café, keys, neighbor's place)
elements.drawn_as: yellow sticky notes with a folded corner and orange outline; c4 grey as already selected; each with an italic index c0 to c5 above

elements.name: Environment
elements.role: the retrieval environment that answers an action with a reward and the next state
elements.drawn_as: white rounded box with a thick light-blue outline and a grey title below

elements.name: reward function / critic
elements.role: computes the reward from the question and the answer
elements.drawn_as: solid blue box with black outline and white text

elements.name: Question and Answer notes
elements.role: the question 'Where could John have forgotten his keys?' (q) and the answer 'cafe, pharmacy' (y)

elements.name: st+1 = q {c3 c4}
elements.role: next state after adding the chosen chunk c3 to the selected set

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw an RL method over text as one closed loop: agent box above, environment box below, the document as a row of sticky-note chunks between them, state and action as small equations of coloured chips, and side arrows that close the cycle.
lessons.suits: RL or agentic methods over a text corpus (retrieval, search, tool use) where the state grows by chunks and agent, environment and data must be visible together.

evidence: Q-RAG agent interacts with multi-step retrieval environment.
The policy πθ selects the next chunk from At with probability proportional to its Qθ(st, ci) value.

summary: Q-RAG fine-tunes the embedder of a retrieval-augmented generator with value-based reinforcement learning so that an agent retrieves chunks of a long context step by step. Figure 1 draws one episode step as an agent-environment loop. In the green Q-RAG Agent box a State Embedder encodes the state (the query q and the already selected chunk c4) and an Action Embedder encodes every chunk; their embeddings give Q values for each chunk and a policy π that selects a_t = c3. A row of yellow sticky-note chunks c0 to c5 under a curly brace, the Long-Context Document, feeds the action embedder. In the blue Environment box a reward function or critic, a question note and an answer note produce r(t+1) and the new state, and arrows close the loop to the next timestep.
summary_zh: Q-RAG用基于价值的强化学习微调嵌入器，让智能体逐步检索长上下文。图1把一步画成智能体-环境循环：状态与各文本块的嵌入得到Q值和策略π，选出块c3；黄色便签块组成长文档；蓝色环境框里的奖励函数/评判器返回奖励与新状态。
notes: Kinds: actor-interaction first as in the pre-screen, model-anatomy for the agent's internals, worked-walkthrough because one step is shown on a toy story. The grey note and the × are read as 'already selected chunk' and 'not scored'; the caption says Q is evaluated for chunks in At. The story about John's keys is likely written for the figure.
